questions.prompt: Which statement best matches the syllabus focus of “Compiling Dart for the Web”?
options: This is exclusively a Flutter widget/rendering concern and has no relationship to Dart language or tooling.
This means disabling static analysis and treating every runtime value as a trusted type.
This is a deployment-only detail that can be ignored while writing and testing source code.
JavaScript output and browser-compatible application considerations
questions.answer_key: JavaScript output and browser-compatible application considerations
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus describes this lesson as: JavaScript output and browser-compatible application considerations.

questions.prompt: Which first step is most useful when applying “Compiling Dart for the Web” in a small Dart program?
options: Copy a dependency version without checking its SDK constraint, maintenance, license, or API documentation.
Assume that a successful native run proves the same APIs and behavior are available on web targets.
Build a minimal Dart example for Compiling Dart for the Web, predict its behavior, and verify an edge case before integrating it.
Change multiple unrelated parts until the output appears plausible, then skip a repeatable test.
questions.answer_key: Build a minimal Dart example for Compiling Dart for the Web, predict its behavior, and verify an edge case before integrating it.
questions.explanation: A minimal example and an explicit boundary check make the behavior easier to verify and maintain.

questions.prompt: If a program involving “Compiling Dart for the Web” behaves unexpectedly, which response is most reliable?
options: Add an unrelated package or a broad refactor before reproducing the reported behavior.
Reduce the failure to a small case, inspect the complete diagnostic and inputs, verify the documented SDK/target constraints, and test one change at a time.
Suppress the diagnostic first and investigate only if a user reports a production failure.
Treat untrusted JSON or command-line input as statically validated simply because the program uses Dart.
questions.answer_key: Reduce the failure to a small case, inspect the complete diagnostic and inputs, verify the documented SDK/target constraints, and test one change at a time.
questions.explanation: Reducing a failure and inspecting full diagnostics avoids speculative changes and exposes SDK/platform assumptions.
